title: Persona quickstarts playbook (brainpad)
body:
High level goal:
- Make it trivial for engineers to pick a pre-baked persona + quickstart that encodes sensible prompts, safety checks, and telemetry so they can ship an initial experience in <1 hour.

Why?
- Customers keep asking for example prompt sets tailored to different user types (support agent, knowledgebot, codex-lite, summarizer).
- Current onboarding requires manual prompt engineering + copy/paste config (error-prone).
- If we provide curated persona quickstarts we can: lower time-to-first-success, standardize safety defaults, and collect comparable signals for model quality across use cases.

Core idea (MVP):
- A small library of "personas" (role + prompt wrappers + guardrails + telemetry hooks) that can be dropped into any hosted API route.
- Each persona ships with: short description, example system/user messages, recommended model/quantization profile, batch size and streaming hint, suggested eval prompt set, and visibility flags (sensitive PII? keep cache?).

User stories (rough):
- As an engineer, I want to choose a persona "support-agent-v1" so my chat route comes pre-configured with a system prompt, a fallback policy and logging fields.
- As an SRE, I want persona defaults to include recommended batch/latency targets so capacity suggestions are sensible.
- As a product manager, I want metrics surfaced per-persona (latency, cost per token, accuracy on eval set) so we can compare.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- "Insert persona" button in route creation that applies system prompt and meta config.
- Persona template repo with 6 entries: support-agent, knowledge-search, summarizer, tutor-lite, code-assistant-safe, reranker-light.
- Telemetry fields appended automatically: persona_id, persona_version, applied_overrides.
- Default safety wrapper added (max response length, banned-content filters, redaction policy).

Design knobs / schema: (flat-ish schema bullet list)
- persona_id (slug)
- version
- short_description
- recommended_model: (string)
- recommended_quant: (string)
- system_prompt (string)
- example_user_prompts (list-of-strings)
- safety_wrapper (string identifier)
- telemetry_tags (list-of-strings)
- mute_cache (bool string: "true"/"false")
- default_batch_hint
- fallback_policy (enum: model_fallback | degraded_output | deny)

Telemetry & metrics to track:
- apply_persona (event) -> persona_id, user_id, route_id
- persona_inference_slo -> p50/p95 latency, tokens-in, tokens-out, model_used
- persona_quality_eval -> pass_rate over persona eval set (daily)
- persona_override -> who/what overrode default prompt

Risks / open questions:
- Ownership and lifecycle of templates: who vets new personas? Proposed: product + applied-ml sign-off.
- Security: some personas might enable potentially dangerous capabilities; need a review gate for "power" personas.
- Versioning: how do we handle breaking changes? Need a migration UI and change-log.
- Caching: by default should we cache prefixes? Might leak across tenants if misconfigured. Default to "no global cache" for persona templates unless explicitly opt-in.

Rollout plan (very rough):
- Alpha (internal): 2 personas (support-agent, summarizer). Gather internal feedback from Solutions Eng.
- Beta (select customers): add tutor-lite and knowledge-search. Add simple UI in Console -> Route -> Templates.
- GA: full set, docs, samples repo, blog post + onboarding flow.

Experiment ideas / data to collect:
- Time-to-first-success metric: time from new route creation -> first successful test call (pass criteria defined per persona).
- Persona-simulated evals: run synthetic prompts against model variants to recommend cheapest model that meets quality threshold.
- A/B: default persona vs custom prompt baseline: track retention and support ticket reduction.

Quick mock wireframe (text):
- Route creation page: [Name] [Model dropdown] [Use persona: dropdown -> choose 'Support agent v1 (recommended for customer support flows)'] [Apply persona -> shows preview system prompt + suggested model + telemetry toggles] [Confirm]
- Persona detail pane: Description, example prompts, model recommendations, 'Try in playground' button, 'Fork and edit'

Implementation notes (backend):
- Persona templates stored in a service (json blobs) with API: GET /personas, GET /personas/:id, POST /personas/:id/apply-route
- When applied, create route-level metadata: persona_id, persona_version, and a copy of the system prompt stored in route config (so edits are explicit).
- Telemetry middleware to attach persona_id on requests and record apply/override events.

Open TODOs (short):
- Define 6 initial persona prompts (ask Maya to draft support-agent examples).
- Spike: auto-eval harness that runs persona evals nightly (ticket PROD-421).
- Decide retention policy for persona usage analytics (30d/90d).
- UX: wireframes for console; assign to Leo for quick mock in Figma.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- Could ship as "Templates" in Console rather than tightly-coupled persona object initially. Easier rollback.
- Allow customers to clone persona into private namespace (private templates) — important for enterprise.
- Consider a "safety tier" flag: low/medium/high which gates model suggestions.
- Need a small playbook for Solutions Eng to customize personas for customers (folder with examples).

Slack refs:
- slack:/C03J2M8Q/thread-: persona quickstarts convo (Nov 2024)

End of brainpad. Need to sync with Maya/Leo and schedule 30m to triage next steps.
summary: Draft brainstorm for a persona-based quickstarts/templates feature for hosted routes: goals, schema, telemetry, MVP acceptance, rollout and TODOs.
